newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Diesel shrugs off crude losses.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Diesel shrugs off crude losses.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps brushed aside the large falls to overnight crude prices late afternoon on Tuesday to trade above Monday's levels on renewed December physical purchases, traders said.
December gas oil swaps traded this afternoon at $30.00, up from Monday's $29.80/29.95, brokers said. This morning December traded at $28.85 and $28.80.
"The market picked on talks of new buying from China and India," one trader said.

December swaps was also boosted by talks of tight supplies as the arbitrage for exports from the west is closed and this led to a widening of the December/January backwardation to 55/60 cents from Monday's 40/50 cents.
December gas oil swaps was last quoted at $30.05/$30.10 with January seen at $29.50/$29.55, brokers said.

Overnight December gas oil futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) closed down $2.00 per tonne to $218.75, and on Tuesday it opened down 25 cents. January Brent lost 43 cents to close at $22.89 a barrel.
Jet fuel rose further this afternoon due to the recent purchases by China and Japan with December jet fuel/gas oil spread quoted at 85 cents/$1.00, up from Monday's 60/80 cents.
Fuel oil swaps picked up on some bottom picking as buyers returned to the market. December traded at $117.50 per tonne and January traded at $116.50, down about $1 from Monday.
Brokers said that sellers had backed off with bids seen for November at $117.25 and December at $117.50.
Naphtha was quoted weaker on the lower crude in very thin trade, with December swaps quoted at $22.65/$22.75, one broker said.
